title: They ran.
paragraphs: They ran.

Boats cut through the water.
Feet pounded the ground.
Eyes locked on one thing—
Bread.
But Jesus saw deeper.

Not the movement.
Not the crowd size.
Not the hype.
He saw the motive.
“You are seeking Me… because you ate your fill of the loaves” (John 6:26).
That is the line that splits the heart open.

Because it means this:
You can chase Jesus… and still not want Him.
Let that sit.

They crossed a sea—but not their sin.
They searched for a miracle—but not for mercy.
They wanted provision—but not transformation.
And if we’re honest?
We’re not far from that crowd.

Some of us pray hardest when we’re in need.
Some of us worship loudest when doors are opening.
Some of us cling to God—not because He is Lord—
—but because He is useful.
Pause.
What are you really following Jesus for?

Is it peace… or His presence?
Blessing… or surrender?
A way out… or a new heart?
Because Jesus didn’t flatter the crowd.
He confronted them.
“Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures to eternal life” (John 6:27).

That’s not a suggestion.
That’s a call to realign your entire soul.
Here’s the tension:

Temporary bread fills your stomach.
But only Christ fills your soul.

And Jesus doesn’t offer Himself as an add-on to your life.
He offers Himself as your life.
“I am the bread of life; whoever comes to Me shall not hunger, and whoever believes in Me shall never thirst” (John 6:35).
This is where everything shifts.

Because the Gospel is not:
“Come to Jesus and He will fix your circumstances.”

The Gospel is:
“Come to Jesus because you are spiritually dead—and He alone can give you life.”
Let’s not soften that.

We were not just hungry people needing help.
We were sinners needing rescue.

Sin isn’t just weakness—it’s rebellion.
Not just brokenness—it’s guilt before a holy God.
And no amount of “bread”—success, relationships, money, even religious activity—can fix that.
Only Jesus.
Only the One who stood before that crowd… and would later hang on a cross.
Think about it.

The same hands that broke bread for thousands…
would be pierced.

The same voice that said “Come to Me”…
would cry, “It is finished.”

The same Savior they chased for food…
would give His flesh for the life of the world (John 6:51).
That’s the scandal.
They wanted bread.
He offered His body.
They wanted a miracle.
He offered a cross.
And many walked away.

Not because Jesus failed them—
but because He refused to be reduced to their expectations.
Read John 6 carefully.
When Jesus began to speak about true discipleship—about eating His flesh and drinking His blood (a metaphor pointing to fully receiving His sacrifice by faith)—many said:
“This is a hard saying; who can listen to it?” (John 6:60)
And then—
they left.

Crowds disappeared.
Followers faded.
Convenience was exposed.
Because shallow faith cannot survive deep truth.
Let me say it plain:

If you follow Jesus only for what He gives,
you will leave Him when He demands your heart.
But then comes one of the most powerful moments in Scripture.
Jesus turns to the Twelve.

No crowd.
No noise.
Just a question:
“Do you want to go away as well?” (John 6:67)
And Peter answers—not perfectly, but truthfully:
“Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life” (John 6:68).
That’s it.
That’s the line between consumers and disciples.
Not perfection.
But surrender.
Not having it all together—
but knowing there is nowhere else to go.
Beloved, hear this with both fire and tenderness:

Jesus is not your supplier.
He is your Savior.

He is not a means to your dreams.
He is the end of your searching.
And yet—
grace still stands.

Because even if you came to Him for the wrong reasons…
even if your prayers were driven by need more than love…
even if your faith has been shallow—
He doesn’t push you away.
He calls you deeper.

He exposes your hunger…
so He can satisfy it with Himself.
This is the invitation:
Come.

Not for bread that spoils.
Not for blessings that fade.
Not for temporary relief.
Come for Him.

Repent—turn from sin, from self, from using God.
Believe—trust in Jesus Christ, crucified and risen.
Receive—not just His gifts, but His Lordship.
And when everything else fails—

when prayers feel unanswered,
when life gets heavy,
when following Him costs you something—
you will still stand and say:
“Lord… where else can I go?”

Because once you have tasted the true Bread—
nothing else satisfies.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
